detail:
The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases describes two connected NIH efforts. RECOVER, launched in 2021, studies how SARS-CoV-2 infection leads to Long COVID and who is at risk, and runs clinical trials on interventions for viral persistence, cognitive dysfunction, autonomic problems affecting heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, and digestion, hypersomnia, and exercise intolerance with post-exertional malaise.

RECOVER-TLC, launched in 2024 and led by NIAID, applies a clinical-trials model to candidate treatments tied to identified biological mechanisms; it began research on baricitinib in March 2026, expanding a trial testing whether it improves thinking and memory problems and reduces fatigue in adults with Long COVID, with trials of three other agents expected to follow. Findings may also inform other infection-associated chronic conditions, including ME/CFS.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor before considering any research study.
sourceVideoTitle: Long COVID and Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (NIAID)
summary: NIH's RECOVER initiative and the newer RECOVER-TLC program run trials aimed at Long COVID's mechanisms, including viral persistence, cognitive dysfunction, autonomic problems, sleep disturbance, and exercise intolerance; there are still no approved therapies for Long COVID itself.
takeaways: recover trials group treatments by symptom cluster
autonomic problems like pots are one named trial area
recover-tlc began testing baricitinib for cognition and fatigue
joining a trial is a personal decision to discuss with your doctor
title: RECOVER: the national Long COVID research effort
